spans.s:
Bandhana denotes a ‘rope’ or other fastening in the Atharvaveda and later.
Foot notes Av. iii. 6, 7 (of a boat, nau); vi. 14, 2.
Śatapatha brāhmaṇa, xiii. 1, 6, 2 (of a horse); taittirīya brāhmaṇa, iii. 8, 9, 4; Chāndogya upaniṣad, vi. 8, 2; nirukta, xii. 38, etc.

Bandhu, denoting ‘relationship’ in the abstract and ‘relation’ in the concrete, occurs in the Rigveda and later.
Foot notes Rv. v. 73, 4; vii. 72, 2; viii. 73, 12, etc.; Av. v. 11, 10, 11; Vājasaneyi Saṃhitā, iv. 22; x. 6, etc.
Rv. i. 164, 33; vii. 67, 9; Av. x. 10, 23; taittirīya brāhmaṇa, iii. 7, 5, 5, etc.; bandhumant, ‘having relations,’ Rv. viii. 21, 4; taittirīya Saṃhitā, i. 5, 1, 4, etc.
